full_judgment: 33. Mr Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Advocate for the ACC, vehemently argues that PW 1 categorically deposed that the money was seized as per order of the appellant. PW 1 and other PWs also deposed that the appellant demanded Taka 50 lakh from PW 1 and others which include Taka 20 lakh already deposited with the police station. When the demand was not met, 3(three) criminal cases were filed against the PW 1 at the instructions of the appellant and he was put in detention under the Special Powers Act, 1974 at the instance of the appellant to create pressure upon the PW 1 to meet his demand. The learned Advocate submits that the appellant was the Superintendent of Police (SP) of Hobiganj district and as such all the events took place with his consent, approval and instructions. The appellant had a dishonest intention from very beginning which can be inferred from the circumstances as it cannot be proved directly. In support of the argument the learned Advocate refers to paragraph 17 at page 4056 of Dr Hari Singh Gour's Penal Law of India 11th edition, Vol. IV which states that dishonest intention must be inferred from circumstances as it cannot be proved directly (Maheshwar Bhanja vs State, 26 Cut. LT 210: ILR (1960) 5 Cut. 143).
